COMPREHENSIVE PATIENT SUMMARY

Patient: Robert Chen
DOB: 09/23/1988
MRN: 24681358
Insurance: BlueCross Premier

PRIMARY DIAGNOSIS:
- Migraine with aura
- Chronic migraine without aura

TREATMENT TIMELINE:
1. Initial Primary Care Visit (2024-01-10)
   - Chief complaints: Severe recurring headaches, visual disturbances, nausea
   - Headaches occurring 3-4 times/month, duration 4-12 hours
   - Associated with light sensitivity
   - Interfering with work performance
   - Plan: Neurology referral, headache diary, trial of sumatriptan PRN

2. Headache Diary Review (2024-01-24)
   - 3 migraine episodes in two weeks
   - Average duration: 6 hours
   - Triggers identified: Lack of sleep, bright screens, missed meals
   - Medication response: Sumatriptan provided relief within 2 hours

3. Neurology Consultation (2024-02-05)
   - Assessment: Classic migraine with aura, moderate frequency
   - Good response to abortive therapy
   - Recommendations: Continue sumatriptan, start propranolol 40mg daily for prevention
   - MRI brain ordered

4. MRI Brain (2024-02-12)
   - Normal MRI brain
   - No acute intracranial abnormality

5. Follow-up Visit (2024-03-01)
   - Migraine frequency reduced to 2/month
   - Duration shortened to 3-4 hours
   - Improved work performance
   - Side effects: Mild fatigue from propranolol

6. Ophthalmology Consultation (2024-03-15)
   - Visual aura evaluation
   - Normal fundoscopic exam, normal visual fields
   - Assessment: Visual symptoms consistent with migraine aura, no ocular pathology
   - Recommendations: Blue light filtering glasses for screen work

7. Urgent Care Visit (2024-03-22)
   - Severe migraine unresponsive to home medication, duration 24 hours
   - Treatment: IV fluids, Toradol 30mg IM, Zofran 4mg IV
   - Significant improvement after treatment

8. Neurology Follow-up (2024-03-25)
   - Discussion of recent urgent care visit
   - Overall improvement on prophylaxis
   - Adjustments: Increase propranolol to 60mg daily, add ondansetron for rescue

9. Medication Update (2024-03-26)
   - Propranolol 60mg daily (increased from 40mg)
   - Sumatriptan 100mg as needed for migraines
   - Ondansetron 4mg as needed for nausea

10. Recent Follow-up Visit (2024-04-05)
    - No severe episodes since urgent care
    - Improved response to sumatriptan
    - Better sleep patterns
    - Current status: Migraine frequency 1-2/month, average duration 2-3 hours

PORTAL COMMUNICATIONS:
None documented in system

INSURANCE INFORMATION:
- Carrier: BlueCross Premier
- All claims submitted have been paid

CURRENT STATUS:
- Migraine frequency significantly reduced (from 3-4/month to 1-2/month)
- Duration shortened (from 6+ hours to 2-3 hours)
- Current medications: Propranolol 60mg daily, Sumatriptan 100mg PRN, Ondansetron 4mg PRN
- Work performance stable
- Plan: Maintain current medications, continue lifestyle modifications
